title: Sonny and the Kangaroo Joey | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka watches a very young kangaroo joey peek out from its mother's pouch in the moonlight — just eyes and ears and a tiny nose, watching the world from the safest place there is. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The mother kangaroo was grazing.

She was tall and grey and patient, pulling at the moonlit grass in long, slow movements. Sunny watched from a respectful distance.

Then she saw the pouch.

Something in the pouch was moving — just slightly — and as Sunny watched, a small pair of ears appeared over the rim. Then eyes. Then a tiny nose.

The joey.

Very young. Barely emerged. It rested its chin on the rim of the pouch and blinked at the world with enormous dark eyes. The world, for now, was the moonlit clearing and its mother's warm grey side.

Sunny kept very still.

The joey looked at her. She looked at the joey. Neither one moved.

It blinked again.

Then its mother moved — one long, slow, grazing hop to the side — and the joey swayed gently inside the pouch with the motion, its ears flattening slightly, then rising again.

Sunny thought: what a thing, to be carried like that. To have the whole world come to you, rocking gently, while you watch from somewhere warm and safe.

The joey's eyes were growing heavy.

She could see it — the lids drooping, the tiny head nodding.

Still resting on the pouch rim, it fell asleep.

Sunny fell asleep too, right there in the soft grass.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little joey. Goodnight, little one.
